standard_prerequisites.use: Identifies the chart D_+(T_0) with the spectrum of k[x, y]/(f) and, via the Jacobian discussion, makes one partial derivative nonzero at the given smooth point.

standard_prerequisites.name: Etale projections and universally bounded fibres
standard_prerequisites.use: Gives the etale projection V -> Spec(k[x]) after shrinking, the openness of its image, and the bound of degree at most d on the fibres since f has degree at most d in y.

core_obligations: Chart reduction (proof lines 1949-1962): at the smooth point z' some partial derivative of f = F(1, x, y) is nonzero; renumbering coordinates puts the nonzero derivative in y, producing a nonempty open V of the chart over which the projection to the affine line is etale.

Degree and rational point (proof lines 1963-1975): the fibres of the projection have degree at most d because f has degree at most d in y; the image U is open in Spec(k[x]), hence contains a k-rational point as k is infinite; any point z of V over it is a smooth closed point with kappa(z)/k finite separable of degree at most d.
proof_roadmap: Move to an affine chart and use the Jacobian criterion to isolate a nonzero partial derivative.
Shrink to the etale locus of the vertical projection.
Bound the fibre degrees by the y-degree of f.
Harvest a rational point in the image over the infinite field and read off separability and the degree bound.

The proof (lines 1949-1975) is complete: the chart reduction with the Jacobian argument, the etale projection from a nonempty open, the fibre-degree bound from the y-degree of f, and the rational-point harvest over the infinite base. Every step is present with no omissions. H2: a clean etale-projection argument with standard bookkeeping.
